indicator_name: Change in water stress levels over time
source_value: This indicator measures change in the level of water stress over time. It is calculated as the ratio between total freshwater withdrawn by all major sectors and total renewable freshwater resources, after taking into account environmental flow requirements. Main sectors, as defined by ISIC standards, include agriculture; forestry and fishing; manufacturing; electricity industry; and services. Data on water withdrawals and total water resources available are commonly collected by national line ministries and institutions (e.g. for Water, Agriculture and Environment) and the National Statistical Office and can be used to assess current status and trends over time.

indicator_name: Proportion of critical water and sanitation infrastructure systems that are built or retrofitted to withstand climate-related hazards
source_value: This indicator measures proportion of critical water and sanitation infrastructure systems that are built or retrofitted to conform with national regulations and standards for climate resilience. Critical water infrastructure refers to essential water-related systems and facilities that have the ability to prevent, protect against, or recover from disasters. This ensures that services essential for the maintenance of vital societal functions, economic activities, public health and safety, or the environment (essential services) are constantly available. Critical water related infrastructure could include among others (and it is not limited to) drinking water suppliers and distributor networks, reservoirs, dams, wastewater collection and treatment plants, electricity production like hydropower, transport on water and flood protection systems, irrigation systems and supporting assets like pumps and control centers. Water and sanitation infrastructure may be considered critical for health, education, agriculture, industry or other purposes. Data on the number and proportion of critical water and sanitation infrastructure systems that are designed, built or retrofitted to withstand climate-related hazards is typically available from National Adaptation Plans, or equivalent policy instruments, and from relevant national line ministries and institutions (e.g. for Water, Agriculture and Environment).
rationale: ADJUDICATED (accepted): ratio structure definable but "critical infrastructure" class boundary unpublished; metadata to be developed

indicator_name: Number of Parties that integrate climate adaptation measures in their national plans for water resources management and water supply and sanitation plans
source_value: This indicator assesses the extent to which national plans for water resources management and water supply and sanitation integrate climate adaptation measures. It builds on established process indicators with existing guidance and system of reporting on progress towards SDG targets. SDG 6.5.1 country survey assesses the degree of integrated water resources management implementation at national level (0-100) and could be expaned to include implementation of climate adaptation measures. The UN-Water Global Analysis and Assessment of Sanitation and Drinking-Water (GLAAS) survey assesses the extent to national water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) plans include climate risk assessment. Adaptation measures are country specific but there are established methods for assessing degrees of implementation.
rationale: ADJUDICATED (accepted): count variable tied to published instruments (SDG 6.5.1 survey, GLAAS); extension not invention
